benefits: The total value of the Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is $820,000
$82,500 contribution to the researcher's salary per annum (excl. GST)
$82,500 in organisational overheads to the host organisation per annum (excl. GST)
$40,000 for research-related expenses per annum (excl. GST)
Fellowships are awarded on a 0.8 Full Time Equivalent basis; the remainder of Fellows' time may be used for other research, teaching and non-research related development opportunities
The Fellowship may be undertaken on a part-time basis to enable family and/or care responsibilities, extending the duration up to a maximum of 8 years with host and Society agreement
eligibility: An early career researcher is a researcher whose PhD was conferred within 4 years of the closing date for applications

The PhD-conferral eligibility period may be extended beyond 4 years at the discretion of the Society for extended sickness leave, part-time employment or career interruptions because of care giving responsibilities, work or service in the community or an industry, or as otherwise agreed by the Society

The applicant must be hosted by a New Zealand-based research organisation that can demonstrate it is capable and willing to provide support and facilities; the host cannot be a department of the public service as listed in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Public Service Act 2020

Applicants must not have previously received substantial research grant funding in a leadership capacity - this means a previous award of either a Marsden Fast Start grant or an Endeavour grant as Principal Investigator or equivalent leadership role (previous award as Associate Investigator or in any other capacity does not disqualify)
An applicant may make only one application for a Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowship in any one funding round

A former successful applicant may not apply for a second Fellowship in the same scheme, and a previous holder of a Rutherford Discovery Fellowship or the James Cook Research Fellowship may not apply for an equivalent Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship
requirements: Register the host organisation as a prospective host in the on-line web-based application system (portal); registration opens at any time
Obtain portal access through the host organisation's research office and submit the proposal on the portal before the closing date (2026 round: 2.00pm NZST, Thursday 9 July 2026)
Complete the Society's application templates: Narrative CV, Visionary statement, Host support, Proposed research and Budget (also available in .odt format; LaTeX is not available)

Nominate referees who are invited by the Society after the closing date; applicant-solicited referee reports must reach the Secretariat by 2.00pm NZST on the published date (2026 round: Thursday 6 August 2026)
documents: Host support template (completed with the host organisation)
selection_criteria: Potential as a future research leader, which may include vision for their field of work, understanding of how their research can benefit New Zealand (including potential benefits in areas of future value, growth or critical need for New Zealand), team leadership and knowledge transfer activity
Good potential to develop and progress their career in research
coverage: Salary contribution of $82,500 per year (excl. GST) to the researcher's salary
Organisational overheads of $82,500 per year (excl. GST) to the host organisation
Research-related expenses of $40,000 per year (excl. GST)
application_method: On-line web-based application system (portal); access arranged through the host organisation's research office
Proposal guidelines and application templates published by the Society

official.description: The New Zealand Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowships support Aotearoa New Zealand's talented early career researchers to establish the foundations of an excellent and impactful research career. They are the early-career scheme of the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, with around 20 fellowships awarded each year.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an employed-researcher fellowship, not a student scholarship: you need a New Zealand host research organisation to sponsor you before you can apply, and the $820,000 is paid to that host as salary contribution, overheads and research expenses across four years. Eligibility is gated on your PhD being conferred within four years of the closing date, plus a rule excluding anyone who has already led major contestable funding as Principal Investigator. With the 2026 round closed on 9 July 2026 and results due late October 2026, the practical move now is to line up a host and draft the five required templates so you are ready when the next round opens (the 2026 round opened on 1 May).
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers 0-4 years post-PhD holding an academic or research appointment at a New Zealand research organisation who need salary, overhead and research funding to establish independence.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your PhD conferral date falls within 4 years of the expected next closing date, and gather evidence now if you need a discretionary extension (illness, caregiving, community or industry service)
Secure a host that can demonstrate capability and willingness to support you - public service departments listed in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Public Service Act 2020 cannot host
Check you have never been PI or equivalent lead on a Marsden Fast Start or Endeavour grant; Associate Investigator roles do not disqualify you
Contact your host's research office early for portal access and start the Narrative CV, Visionary statement, Host support, Proposed research and Budget templates
Line up referees well before the July closing date - applicant-solicited reports have their own deadline about a month after applications close
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a confirmed host: portal access comes through the host research office, so a missing Host support template kills the bid
Falling outside the PhD-conferral window or having led a Marsden Fast Start or Endeavour grant as PI - both are hard eligibility bars, not discretionary

A visionary statement that reads as an ordinary research proposal instead of a leadership vision, since panellists score potential as a future research leader (vision, benefit to New Zealand, team leadership, knowledge transfer)
Referee reports arriving after the separate referee deadline, not the application deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any host-side costs beyond the $82,500 per year organisational overheads, plus teaching and administrative duties outside the 0.8 FTE research commitment, are carried by the host rather than the fellowship.
document_audit: The Host support template must be completed with your host, not written by you alone - start that conversation months before the round opens
Templates are supplied by the Society in Word and .odt formats only (no LaTeX), and a Narrative CV is mandatory rather than a conventional publication list
Referees are applicant-solicited and invited only after the closing date, so brief them in advance on the deadline they will face
alerts: Only one application per funding round is allowed, and a prior Tāwhia te Mana success in the same scheme, a Rutherford Discovery Fellowship or a James Cook Research Fellowship blocks an equivalent application
Fellows must commence their programme of research within 12 months of award notification
The fellowship runs at 0.8 FTE by default; agreeing a reduced FTE pro-rates the salary, overhead and research-expense amounts
Around 20 Fellowships are awarded annually against hundreds of eligible applications, so a strong host commitment and referee backing matter as much as the research idea
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Host registers in the portal, the applicant builds the five templated sections with host sign-off, submits through the portal by the 2.00pm NZST closing date, then solicited referee reports follow about a month later.

benefits: 5 vocational education and training (VET) scholarships, each valued at $10,000 for study of a minimum of 120 credits at NZQA level 4 to 7 non-degree
4 undergraduate scholarships, each valued up to $30,000 ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 3 years)
3 master's scholarships valued up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
1 Master of Education research scholarship valued up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
1 doctoral scholarship valued up to $40,000 ($20,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
14 scholarships are awarded each year after the 2026 to 2027 Budget increased Fund funding by $100,000 each year, adding 5 scholarships
eligibility: Of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi
Enrolling in, or already enrolled to continue, full-time tertiary study for the academic year the scholarship supports (the page states the 2027 academic year for the closed round)
VET applicants: the course leads to a certificate or diploma at NZQA levels 4 to 7, is at least 120 credits total, and is studied, trained or undertaken as an apprenticeship full time
VET applicants must not be doing a bachelor's degree - bachelor's students apply for the Ngarimu undergraduate scholarship instead
Level 4 apprenticeship applicants must have completed years 1 to 2 of their apprenticeship and be enrolling in their third or fourth subsequent year
Preference will be given to applicants whose studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori
requirements: Submit the online application form on the Ministry of Education Ngarimu scholarships page when applications are open
Be enrolled in the course in the year the scholarship money is paid - the Ministry states 'if you apply for the scholarship in 2026, you will get the money for the scholarship in 2027'
Apprentices who move to a new employer can keep receiving the scholarship as long as they stay enrolled in that apprenticeship
Read the Ngarimu scholarships application guidance published by the Ministry
documents: Record of achievement or other record of learning - a MyBCITO record, a transcript from the tertiary provider, an NZQA record of achievement for NCEA or other NZQA qualification results, or another record of learning from the course provider

For undergraduate applicants yet to start study: an NZQA record of learning for NCEA Level 2 (and Level 3 if applicable) or equivalent Cambridge International Examinations or International Baccalaureate results

Reference or endorsement commenting on academic achievement and suitability for study or training, from someone involved in the applicant's study or training journey (lecturer, tutor, secondary school staff member, workplace assessor, teacher, dean, community leader, church minister) - it cannot be from a friend or family member
Master's and Master of Education research applicants: a brief statement of up to 250 words outlining the topic, reasons for interest in the subject area and future expectations
Doctoral applicants: a 500-word essay outlining the topic of the thesis/doctorate and future expectations
Doctoral applicants: a reference from the chief supervisor commenting on academic abilities, commitment and contribution to the area of study, and confirming acceptance into the PhD programme
selection_criteria: A selection panel assesses applications from exceptional Māori students who demonstrate values that align with the values of the 28th Māori Battalion
The panel gives preference to applicants who demonstrate that their studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori
coverage: VET scholarships: $10,000 each for study of a minimum of 120 credits at NZQA level 4 to 7 non-degree
Undergraduate scholarships: up to $30,000 each ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 3 years)
Master's scholarships: up to $20,000 each ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
Master of Education research scholarship: up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
Doctoral scholarship: up to $40,000 ($20,000 per year of full-time study for up to 2 years)
application_method: Online application form published on the Ministry of Education Ngarimu scholarships page when the annual window opens
Ngarimu scholarships application guidelines PDF published by the Ministry
official.application_route: Complete the online application form on the Ministry of Education Ngarimu scholarships page during the annual application window.
official.study_mode: Full-time tertiary study, training or apprenticeship (enrolling or continuing)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi
official.international_eligibility: No separate international-student rule is published; undergraduate applicants yet to begin study may evidence NCEA Level 2 (and Level 3 if applicable) or equivalent Cambridge International Examinations or International Baccalaureate results

official.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are awarded every year by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established in 1945 by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Act 1945, to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values that align with the values of the 28th Māori Battalion. The Board was set up to promote the study and maintenance of te reo Māori, Māori history, Māori tradition and Māori culture, and following a $100,000 per year funding increase from the 2026 to 2027 Budget it now awards 14 scholarships each year.
official.program_type: Merit scholarship scheme across vocational, undergraduate, master's and doctoral levels

applicant_utility.summary: This is a values-and-whakapapa based award rather than a pure marks contest: you must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi, and the panel gives preference to study that improves the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori, so your statement should make that link explicit. Pick the right scheme first - bachelor's students must use the undergraduate award, not the VET one, and each level carries its own essay or statement requirement. The money is paid the year after you apply, so an application lodged in 2027 funds 2028 study and you must still be enrolled in that year. With the 2027 round closed on 19 July 2026 and outcomes due late November 2026, the next window opens mid-2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Māori students entering or continuing full-time vocational, undergraduate, master's or doctoral study in New Zealand who can evidence achievement and alignment with the values of the 28th Māori Battalion.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which of the five schemes you fit (VET, undergraduate, master's, Master of Education research, doctoral) before starting - bachelor's students are excluded from the VET award
Apprentices: confirm you have completed years 1 to 2 of a level 4 apprenticeship and are enrolling in your third or fourth subsequent year
Request an NZQA record of achievement or verified tertiary transcript early; international-school leavers should request their CIE or IB records as NCEA equivalents
Ask a lecturer, tutor, workplace assessor or community leader (never a friend or family member) for the reference or endorsement well before the window opens
Draft the 250-word (master's) or 500-word (doctoral) statement around how your study improves the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori
Plan around payment timing: apply one year, get paid the next, and stay enrolled in the year the money is paid
common_rejection_risks: Whakapapa or Māori descent not evidenced, or the wrong scheme entered (a bachelor's student applying under the VET award)
A reference from a friend or family member, or an endorsement that does not comment on suitability for study or training
Statements that ignore the wellbeing-of-Māori preference the panel is instructed to apply
Not being enrolled in the year the money is paid - the Ministry pays the following year and requires continued enrolment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Awards are fixed values rather than full-cost coverage, so tuition fees, living costs, course materials and travel beyond the award value must be met from other sources; the Ministry does not state that payments are applied to fees.
document_audit: Doctoral applicants need two separate documents: a 500-word essay and a chief-supervisor reference that also confirms acceptance into the PhD programme
VET applicants can evidence a MyBCITO record instead of a formal transcript, but it must show the full 120-credit course
Undergraduates yet to start study use NCEA records (or CIE/IB equivalents) - a tertiary transcript only applies once study has begun
The Master of Education research scholarship is specifically for candidates planning Māori education research, so a generic education topic will not match the scheme
alerts: Applications closed 19 July 2026 for 2027 study and reopen only mid-2027 for 2028 study - there is a long gap between rounds
Moving employer mid-apprenticeship does not forfeit the award provided enrolment continues
Only 14 awards are made each year across five schemes and some schemes receive a single award, so check which scheme gives you the best odds
Outcomes for the closed 2027 round are not expected until late November 2026, so have a fallback funding plan for the 2027 study year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online form on the Ministry of Education page during the annual window, attach the record of achievement and reference (plus the scheme statement or essay), then await notification of the outcome by email.
